verifiers.claim: A run is recorded before it starts and takes one terminal transition; on restart an open run is failed from SQLite with an explicit reason and nothing is re-executed.
On the running example: a run ended once is not cancellable (409), and after the app restarts with its data every run keeps its status and every thread replays unchanged.
A run interrupted mid-effect resumes against recorded inputs instead of failing.
verifiers.reason: resumption needs the lease and receipt-replay protocol of SPEC §4: node --test test/agent/resume.test.ts

verifiers.claim: Start, admission, observation, a concurrent human write, revocation, cancellation and commit interleave freely; a receipt never arises from stale, revoked or stopped work.

A tool's arguments naming another actor, thread or run change nothing: the effect is issued by the loop; a mutating tool runs only while the host says the run is active, and a refusal leaves a refused receipt.
The tool set offered to the model equals declared helper tools intersected with host-allowed tools, changes when either changes, and a declared tool without a handler is refused at load.
Each tool call leaves a receipt with actor, thread, run, tool and the revisions it produced; a transcript claiming more calls changes nothing.
On the running example: the summariser's lookup call leaves a receipt with actor, thread, run and tool, readable in the records the runtime keeps.
A file write through the run's tool lands in the receipt row with mount, path and the revisions before and after, taken from the provider's receipt.
ask and approval rows accept one answer by compare-and-set from the session's actor; an approval for revision n does not cover n+1.
verifiers.reason: decisions are not implemented yet: node --test test/agent/decisions.test.ts

verifiers.claim: No receipt is taken after revocation or cancellation in any interleaving.
Cancelling mid-run stops before the next effect; committed receipts remain; the late output is not committed; a pending run is cancelled without a model call; a run ends once.
A provider credential given at mount time appears in no definition, manifest, run record, event or SQLite file.
allowedTools, mayRequest and isActive are asked at each operation and a host that answers no is obeyed there; an actor sees only their own threads, runs and jobs.
The grants a definition's files: needs produce against the host's mounts are handed to mayRequest for every run.
Changing the host's answers for an actor changes the tools offered; the runtime source compares no role string.
Mounts come from host.mounts per effect and file tools and page commands are offered only when the host allows them by name; the runtime compares no role string.
Each model response writes one usage row attributed to actor, thread, run, agent and model, the host receives it before the next model call, and a host that refuses stops the run.
On the running example: every completed run has a usage row naming actor, agent and model.
Three concurrent submissions over one key and two bodies, with a restart while in flight: same key and body always name one run, another body is refused, and a key creates at most one run.
The same key with the same request returns the recorded run; the same key with another request is a conflict; keys are scoped to the actor.
On the running example over HTTP: the same key with the same body returns the recorded run, another body is 409.

Concurrent requests with one key create one run, one job or one message: the key is reserved synchronously before any await; a request that fails frees its key; another body under a reserved key is a conflict.

Two child slots over declared and undeclared agents: an undeclared plan is refused before any child is recorded, children are recorded from the frozen plan only, a child runs only under its running parent, the parent completes only from completed children, a terminal parent leaves no open child, and a child's terminal status is never rewritten.
A job plans only agents its JOB.md declares; a plan naming another agent is refused before anything is recorded; the parent completes only from completed children.
On the running example: the digest job starts one summarise child per note, completes only when both completed, and an empty plan is 400.

A page command is offered only when the definition names it, the host allows it and a page registered it on the thread; running it is a request record answered once by that page for that actor, expired on timeout, ended unavailable when the page leaves or moves target; a registration cannot shadow a backend tool; the request and its answer replay by cursor.
